newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABARE lowers forecast for Australian cotton.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABARE lowers forecast for Australian cotton.

text.p: The Australian cotton industry should achieve a record lint harvest in 1996/97, rising 24.9 percent to 526,000 tonnes from the 421,000 tonnes produced last year, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.

The forecast, contained in ABARE's September quarter commodities report, was below the 534,0000 tonnes forecast in the June quarter. "Current Australian forward contract prices for cotton, at around A$440/bale (500 lb), are lower than the season average of A$535/bale in 1995-97," ABARE said.
"Despite lower prices, cotton plants are forecast to reach a record 371,000 hectares, assisted in most growing areas by the best supplies of irrigation water for several years," it said.
"Assuming normal seasonal conditions and average yields, a record harvest of 526,000 tonnes (lint) is in prospect for 1996/97," the forecaster said.

ABARE said world cotton prices were forecast to fall by 15.1 percent in 1996/97 to average 73 U.S. cents per pound from 86 cents in 1995/96, with a related rise in world consumption to 19.3 million tonnes from 18.8 million tonnes in 1995/96.
World production, however, was forecast to fall by 0.2 million tonnes in 1996/97 to 19.5 million tonnes with the largest decline in China.
